findings.description: Primary objective unmet and REGRESSED (== INS-2-003, unresolved). Warm crown lnlike re-measured at 27.4 ms (best-of-7, threads pinned) — far above the 10 ms hard target / 15 ms ceiling and worse than the prior build's 18.8 ms. The coarse node grid grew to crown 62 / near-cusp 60 / well-sep 91 / near-fold 83 / sheared 58 (1.1-1.7x vs the 100-node baseline), so lever A (target ~10x fewer nodes) is inverted: accuracy was bought by ADDING nodes. The code's own `_coarse_w_node_grid` docstring concedes ~50-60 nodes are required and that removing the in-kernel oscillation upstream is 'out of scope for this interpolation layer'. No lever-B `_surrogate.py` module and no DATA_CONTRACTS artifact were created.
findings.suggested_fix: Escalate to the owner: with the accuracy gate binding at ~50-60 nodes, lever A alone cannot reach 10-15 ms — this is the brief's step-rule case. Report the measured 27.4 ms / grown-grid floor honestly (do not widen the timing ceiling), and take the residual gap via lever B (the post-contraction 3D surrogate table + DATA_CONTRACTS entry) in a follow-up build. Do not touch the engine layer.
